transcription.original_script:
№ 8
Сероцкѣ
Состоялось въ Посадѣ Сероцкѣ Десятаго (Двадцать втораго
Марта, тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года въ десять
часовъ утра. — Явился лично Моисеева Закона Файбишъ Розен-
бергъ работникъ тридцати одинъ лѣтъ отъ роду, здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ жи-
тельствующій, въ присутствіи свидѣтелей Моисеева Закона Мор-
тка Фишмана мясника, сорока четырехъ лѣтъ отъ роду и
Меера Перельмана работника, сорока лѣтъ отъ роду,
здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ жительствующихъ, и предъявилъ намъ
младенца женскаго пола, объявляя, что она родилась здѣсь въ
Сероцкѣ втораго (четырнадцатаго) Марта текущаго года,
въ три часа ночью отъ законной его жены Сурой, урожденной Ва-
нанки Двадцати пяти лѣтъ отъ роду. — Младенцу
этому дано имя Бруха. — Актъ сей объявляющему и свидѣ-
тельствующимъ прочитанъ и затѣмъ объявляющимъ, свидѣ-
тельствующимъ, а также нами подписанъ.
Фаибишъ Розенбергъ    Meier Perelman
Мортка Фишманъ
Содержащій Акты Гражданскаго Состоянія
transcription.translation: No. 8. Serock. It took place in the Posad of Serock on the tenth (twenty-second) of March, one thousand eight hundred seventy-seven, at ten o'clock in the morning. There appeared in person Fajbisz Rozenberg, of the Mosaic faith, laborer, thirty-one years of age, residing here in Serock, in the presence of the witnesses, of the Mosaic faith, Mortka Fiszman, butcher, forty-four years of age, and Mejer Perelman, laborer, forty years of age, both residing here in Serock, and he presented to us an infant of female sex, declaring that she was born here in Serock on the second (fourteenth) of March of the current year, at three o'clock at night, of his lawful wife Sura, née Wa[...]nka, twenty-five years of age. This infant was given the name Brucha. This act was read to the declarant and the witnesses, and was thereupon signed by the declarant, by the witnesses, and also by us. Fajbisz Rozenberg. Meier Perelman. Mortka Fiszman. Keeper of the Registers of Civil Status.

notes: CONTRADICTS THE BATCH BRIEF, which pins target.language = "pl". Russian in pre-reform orthography throughout the clerk's text.
Two of the three autographs are Cyrillic and one is Latin script.
Read at 6x over source (900,1212,630,58). A coarser band pass suggested Осьмаго; at 6x the opening shows a д-loop then е then с, which gives Десятаго.
The gap check decides in favour of Десятаго: the Gregorian side reads Двадцать втораго, i.e. 22, and 22 minus 12 is 10. Осьмаго would require Двадцатаго.
Sequence check: act 7 registers on 11 February and this act on 10 March, so the register runs in order.
Month name split across the line 1/2 break; quoted across the break as inked. Gap of 12 days is correct.
Both day-words physically inked.

registration_year.original_script: тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года въ десять

notes: Split across the line 2/3 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Surname split across the line 3/4 break; quoted across the break as inked. Read at 6.5x over source (1000,1306,530,58) and 6x over (476,1353,620,58).
Corroborated by the first autograph in the signature block, Фаибишъ Розенбергъ in Cyrillic, read at 3.9x over source (476,1960,1054,145).

NOTABLE: a man of this exact name serves as witness 1 on acts 1, 4, 5 and 6 of this same register year. Here he is the declarant and father, registering his own child, and his usual fellow witness Mortka Fiszman witnesses for him. That is a coherent picture, but see declarant.occupation and declarant.age, where the details do NOT match the witness appearances. Whether this is one man or two of the same name is left for adjudication.
Standard declarant-is-father construction. The word отецъ is not used.
Read at 6x over source (476,1353,620,58) as работникъ. The two candidate words are close in this hand: работникъ and сапожникъ share the -никъ tail and both have a descender in the middle.

The fork matters because acts 1, 4, 5 and 6 all give a Fajbisz Rozenberg as сапожникъ. If this act says работникъ, then either there are two men of the name or the clerk changed the trade word; if it says сапожникъ, it is the same man throughout.
Recorded as the fork rather than harmonised to the register's expectation, since letting the expectation choose is how the act 7 witness misreading happened.
тридцати is firm; the unit word reads одинъ, which is also grammatically irregular after тридцати and so is a little suspect.

Age-continuity tension: the Fajbisz Rozenberg who witnesses acts 1, 4, 5 and 6 is given as 39 or 40. Thirty-one on this act is an eight or nine year gap, which the guidance says is a misread or a different person, not a fact to be smoothed over. Thirty-nine is retained as the alternative precisely because it would reconcile them.
Flagged rather than decided.
Split across the line 4/5 break. Agrees with the margin annotation and the birthplace.
Same person as the declarant.
Either reading sits comfortably with the mother's stated 25.
Split across the line 5/6 break; quoted across the break as inked. Read at 5.5x over source (476,1494,700,58).
Sixth appearance of this witness in the group, after acts 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6, with the same trade every time. Corroborated by the Cyrillic autograph Мортка Фишманъ.
The surname carries the clerk's underline diacritic under the ш.

witness_1.age.original_script: мясника, сорока четырехъ лѣтъ отъ роду и
notes: Excerpt anchored on the trade word and carried through и because the act states two ages beginning сорока.
Witness-age continuity: 44 here as on acts 1, 3, 4 and 5, in a March act as in the January ones. Clean.
Plural phrase covering both witnesses.
The surname Перельмана is firm, read at 5.5x over source (476,1494,700,58). The given name is not: the body form reads about as well as Маска as Меера.
The Latin autograph reads Meier Perelman, which is what puts Mejer first. A new witness, not appearing elsewhere in acts 1 to 8.
Body form is genitive after въ присутствіи свидѣтелей; the autograph is nominative.
Same trade word as read for the declarant on this act, which is one reason the declarant's работникъ reading is not simply discarded.
A bare decade word with no unit word.

Written large by the clerk and straddling the middle of the line, so it was read from both band halves and confirmed at that scale. The -руха tail is firm; the opening capital is the loop group that serves Б, В and Г in this hand.
A female name, consistent with the stated female sex.

Worth noting beside act 7, whose mother's maiden name I read as Прухъ: the two tokens are similar and an adjudicator should check them against each other, but they sit in different slots on different acts and I have not merged them.
Stated explicitly, and corroborated by the feminine что она родилась, by the female name Brucha, and by the absence of circumcision wording in the naming slot.
Gap check: 2 to 14 March is 12 days, correct.
Date arithmetic against the registration: born 2 March Julian, registered 10 March Julian, so registration follows the event by eight days. Consistent, and no delay clause appears.
Both day-words inked, parenthesis closed.
текущаго года, marking an in-time registration.
ночью rather than ночи; recorded as inked.

child.birthplace.original_script:
она родилась здѣсь въ
Сероцкѣ втораго
notes: Split across a line break; quoted through the following day-word to keep it unique. Agrees with the margin annotation.
Read at 7.5x over source (1130,1682,400,58). The clerk inflects it as Сурой here rather than leaving it uninflected as he does on most other acts; the nominative is Сура.
Not the same woman as act 3's Сура Итта or act 5's mother: different maiden name and different age.
Highest-value field on the act and poorly served. The surname breaks across the line 11/12 boundary, which on this page is also the page edge, so the join falls into the gutter shadow.
What is firm: the née marker урожденной, then a В/Б/Х-group capital plus a, then at the start of the next line a token ending -нки. What is lost is whatever stands between.

None of the three candidates is a surname I can vouch for, which is itself a signal that the join is wrong rather than that the surname is unusual. Recorded as read rather than replaced by a plausible-sounding name.
Note the -нки ending is a genitive of -нка, so this is a plain feminine surname form rather than one of the -овны patronymics seen on acts 3, 5 and 6.

mother.age.original_script: нанки Двадцати пяти лѣтъ отъ роду
notes: Read at 6x over source (476,1729,620,58).
The naming slot runs from Младенцу этому straight to дано имя Бруха, with no rite phrase: neither при обрѣзаніи, which would be wrong for a girl, nor при религіозномъ обрядѣ, which would be right.
BLANK rather than ABSENT_ON_FORM: the formula has the slot and this clerk fills it on acts 1, 2, 3 and 6, all male births.
Verified by reading both halves of the line band across the junction with the preceding line, to be sure the phrase had not been carried over the break.

This is now the fourth female birth in the group, on acts 4, 5, 7 and 8, and the rite phrase is missing on every one of them, while every male birth carries при обрѣзаніи. The omission is systematic and therefore informative rather than accidental.

This act uses свидѣтельствующимъ where the other acts in the group use свидѣтелями. A within-register wording variant, recorded as inked and not normalised.
Autographs: Фаибишъ Розенбергъ and Мортка Фишманъ in Cyrillic, Meier Perelman in Latin script, read at 3.9x over source (476,1960,1054,145).
